newsitem.title: USA: Pharmacia says FDA clears Mirapex.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia says FDA clears Mirapex.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration gave Pharmacia & Upjohn Co marketing clearance for sale of Mirapex tablets to treat Parkinson's disease.
Mirapex is the first new Parkinson's drug cleared by the FDA since 1989, said the Swedish-American drug company.
Mirapex will be co-marketed in the United States by Pharmacia and Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals Inc.
"Mirapex will provide another option for Parkinson's patients to improve their daily living functions," said Mark Corrigan, a Pharmacia vice president.
Pharmacia and Boehringer Ingelheim have worked together since 1991 on the development of the drug synthesized by Boehringer Ingelheim, Pharmacia said.
Mirapex is a dopamine agonist shown in trials to be useful in treating patients who have idiopathic Parkinson's disease in early and advanced stages of the disease, Pharmacia said.
"Mirapex can be used with other Parkinson's medications," Corrigan said.

The most frequently reported side effects of patients in early Parkinson's disease who were treated with Mirapex were nausea, dizziness, drowsiness and insomnia. The most common side effects reported by advanced-stage Parkinson's patients treated with Mirapex and levodopa, were postural hypotension, dyskinesias, extrapyramidal syndrome, insomnia, dizziness and hallucinations, Pharmacia said.

"All Parkinson's patients should be informed that postural hypotension may occur more frequently during initial treatment, and hallucinations can occur at any time during the course of treatment," Pharmacia said.
Pharmacia and Boehringer Ingelheim plan to begin distribution of Mirapex to U.S. pharmacies by July 10
Germany's Boehringer Ingelheim is privately held.
